observations: A large black circular form dominates the upper half, its white interior holding two tightly wound gold spiral coils side by side, with a smaller third spiral below them at center.
Black scribbled lines radiate outward across a flat teal background in all directions, crossing and layering without resolving into recognizable shapes.
A black torso below the circle carries a gold diamond shape at its chest, flanked by thin limbs; the lower right corner holds a small white artist mark.
reading: The two gold spirals sit inside a white void ringed by black, drawing the eye inward while the surrounding teal field is crossed by loose, restless lines that never settle. The contrast between the coiled stillness at center and the scattered marks outside reads as tension held just short of release. A small third spiral and a chest diamond repeat the coil motif at reduced scale, giving the figure an internal logic the background refuses to share.

nnotb #119 shares the black-silhouette-on-single-color structure and places small repeated marks where eyes would be, but uses flat xx symbols rather than the wound spiral coils that give #120 its inward pull.

lookingQuestion: The gold spirals sit inside a white area while the teal field outside is covered in loose crossing lines — what does the boundary between those two zones do to how you move through the image?
ambiguities: Whether the scribbled lines in the background are a separate layer over the teal or drawn directly into it cannot be confirmed from the image alone.
The third smaller spiral at lower center of the white area is partially obscured by overlapping black marks, making its exact form uncertain.
